title: Ninth commandment (CCC 2517–2533)
hook: purity of heart lets us see God in others

segments.voice: Yesterday, truth and beauty: real beauty can tell the truth. Your line was beauty is true.

A smudge on a pair of glasses. The wearer doesn't notice it at first. The world just seems a little gray, a little blurred at the edges, and faces look tired. Then the glasses come off, get a wipe on a shirt, go back on, and everything is sharp again. Nothing out there changed. The lens did. The ninth commandment, in the Catechism, turns out to be about lenses: what we look at people through.
screen: `A SMUDGE ON YOUR GLASSES.` → `NOTHING OUT THERE CHANGED.` → `THE LENS DID.`

segments.voice: As the Catechism counts them, the ninth commandment forbids coveting a neighbor's wife: disordered desire, which it calls concupiscence. But it builds the whole section on a line from the Sermon on the Mount, in the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed are the clean of heart: for they shall see God." The heart here isn't just feelings. The Catechism calls it the seat of the moral personality; in plain words, where intentions are born. The pure of heart have tuned mind and will to God's ways, in charity, chastity, love of truth and faith. Then the promise opens in a surprising direction. Seeing God is the end of the road, but purity of heart lets us see according to God now: the other person as a neighbor, and the human body, ours and others', as a temple of the Holy Spirit. That's the smudge wiped off. Not a refusal to look at people, but a way of looking that doesn't reduce them. How does a heart get clean? The Catechism names a struggle and its helps: chastity, purity of intention, purity of vision, discipline over what feelings and imagination dwell on, and prayer. It adds modesty, which protects the private center of a person and refuses to unveil what should stay hidden. And it's grace as well as effort: no one cleans the lens entirely alone. The ninth commandment is less a list of things not to see than a promise about what you'll be able to see.
screen: `BLESSED ARE THE CLEAN OF HEART.` · `THE HEART: WHERE INTENTIONS ARE BORN.` · `SEE OTHERS AS GOD SEES THEM.` · `CHASTITY, INTENTION, VISION, PRAYER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind three faces: someone you love, someone you pass every day without really seeing, and someone you find hard. One at a time, set down the label you usually put on them and look for the person underneath. If you pray, ask to see each one as God sees them; if not, simply let them be more than you thought.
Purity of heart. A heart tuned to God in love, chastity, truth and faith, which, in Catholic teaching, begins to see others, and God, clearly. Today's word.
Your line: they shall see god. A clean heart changes what the eyes can see. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics pray for purity of heart and examine their thoughts and looks before confession; the Church teaches chastity, modesty, purity of intention and prayer as helps in this struggle.

chat.says: Does being 'pure of heart' mean never noticing anyone attractive?
options: Not in the Catechism: it's a way of seeing people whole, as neighbors, with the body as a temple.
Yes. Any glance at an attractive person breaks the ninth commandment, even without wanting anything.
It means avoiding other people's company, so that the heart is never tempted at all.

notes: CCC paraphrased throughout (copyrighted translation). Check: heart as seat of the moral personality (2517); the pure of heart attuned in charity, chastity, love of truth and orthodoxy of faith (2518); seeing 'according to God', the body as temple (2519); the four helps (2520); modesty protecting the intimate center of the person (2521).
Index title cites CCC 2517–2533; the section opens at 2514 (Exodus 20:17 and Matthew 5:28). 'As the Catechism counts them' acknowledges the Catholic numbering of the commandments.
'Faith' stands in for CCC 2518's 'orthodoxy of faith'; confirm.
Editor: hook recast in the third person so it no longer tells the listener what they think or notice.

Editor (second pass): 'four helps' count removed (CCC 2520 lists more than four: chastity, purity of intention, purity of vision, discipline of feelings and imagination, refusing complicity in impure thoughts, prayer); 'desire that treats a person as something to take' replaced with CCC 2514's own word, concupiscence; 'where intentions are born' marked as the lesson's gloss.

Audit (1132–1141 pass): no changes. Matthew 5:8 (Douay-Rheims), Greek καθαροὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, and CCC 2514–2521 (seat of moral personality, seeing 'according to God', body as temple, the helps, modesty) checked and found accurate. The practice (seeing people whole) sits near day 1130's; the lens image and three-faces structure keep it distinct.
